title: About Me

Data Source
The data used in this project combines personal listening metrics with audio feature data sampled from the Spotify catalog (sourced via TidyTuesday’s Spotify songs dataset and Spotify’s Web API). The dataset includes acoustic measurements such as tempo (beats per minute), energy levels, valence (musical positiveness), and track popularity scores, allowing for detailed comparisons between my top 5 most-played songs, similar and contrasting reference tracks, and a wider landscape of 5,000 catalog songs.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/mireillegmz24-glitch/spotify-final

title: Song Comparisons
text:
1. Within the Top 5
All five core songs share a focused musical identity, but each brings distinct nuances:

SQUEEZE (Dominic Fike): Tempo 86 BPM, Energy 52. The most energetic of the Top 5, pairing punchy alternative drum patterns with relaxed vocals.
Oh Yeah? (Steve Lacy): Tempo 92 BPM, Energy 48, Valence 65. The brightest and most upbeat song in the group, driven by warm funk basslines and high musical optimism.
WALLFLOWER (Dominic Fike): Tempo 82 BPM, Energy 44, Valence 38. A more melancholic, guitar-driven bedroom pop record with contemplative pacing.
Give You the World (Steve Lacy): Tempo 78 BPM, Energy 45. A slow-burn, soulful ballad with vintage R&B chord progressions and intimate falsetto.
Evergreen [Stripped] (Omar Apollo): Tempo 75 BPM, Energy 30. The softest and most acoustic track in the group, relying on minimal guitar backing and raw vocal vulnerability.

Shared Core: Moderate tempos (75–92 BPM), low-to-medium energy (30–52), and organic guitar or bass instrumentation that prioritizes vocal intimacy over heavy electronic production.

title: Song Comparisons
section: 2. Top 5 vs. Similar Tracks (R&B & Bedroom Pop)
text:
2. Top 5 vs. Similar Tracks (R&B & Bedroom Pop)

Similar Songs: White Ferrari (Frank Ocean), Japanese Denim (Daniel Caesar), Roommates (Malcolm Todd), and Apocalypse (Cigarettes After Sex).
Similarities: Like the Top 5, these tracks feature introspective lyrics, warm organic instrumentation, and avoid harsh compression or abrasive synthesizers.
Differences:

Pacing & Rhythm: Tracks like White Ferrari (60 BPM, Energy 18) and Apocalypse (Valence 18) lean deeper into slow, ambient melancholy. The Top 5 tracks maintain slightly more rhythmic bounce and groove, making them easier to repeat throughout the day.
Tempo Variation: Japanese Denim pushes to 110 BPM while maintaining low energy (42), whereas the Top 5 stays tightly clustered under 95 BPM.

title: Song Comparisons
section: 3. Top 5 vs. Dissimilar Tracks (Uptempo Pop, Dance & Trap)
text:
3. Top 5 vs. Dissimilar Tracks (Uptempo Pop, Dance & Trap)

Dissimilar Songs: good 4 u (Olivia Rodrigo), Blinding Lights (The Weeknd), Closer (Ne-Yo), and After Party (Don Toliver).
Differences:

Tempo: High-speed tempos ranging from 126 to 171 BPM, compared to the Top 5’s relaxed 75–92 BPM.
Energy: Intense energy levels between 66 and 77, driven by heavily compressed kicks, high-gain synthesizers, and loud mastering.
Listening Function: These tracks are engineered for high-arousal settings like workouts, driving, or parties. While effective in short bursts, their high sensory demand contrasts sharply with the comforting, low-fatigue profile of the Top 5.

title: The Story Behind My Top 5
text:
Research & Audio Analysis

1. The Sweet Spot: Why These Top 5 Dominate
Looking at the musical attributes, the Top 5 tracks (SQUEEZE, Oh Yeah?, WALLFLOWER, Give You the World, and Evergreen) cluster closely together in a distinct “pocket”: - Tempo: A relaxed, head-nodding tempo between 75 and 92 BPM. - Energy: Moderate to low energy levels between 30 and 52, avoiding overwhelming loudness. - Atmosphere: Warm, guitar-driven indie R&B and bedroom pop where vocal tone and emotional intimacy are foregrounded.


2. Comparisons to Similar Songs
Tracks like Frank Ocean’s White Ferrari, Daniel Caesar’s Japanese Denim, Malcolm Todd’s Roommates, and Cigarettes After Sex’s Apocalypse sit very close to the Top 5 cluster: - Shared Qualities: They share organic instrumentation, introspective lyricism, and restrained production. - Why Top 5 Ranks Higher: While White Ferrari and Apocalypse lean heavily into slow, ambient melancholy (tempo down to 60 BPM), the Top 5 tracks maintain slightly more rhythmic bounce and soulful groove (e.g., Steve Lacy’s funk basslines and Dominic Fike’s alternative rhythm), making them easier to replay daily.


3. Contrasting with Dissimilar Songs
Songs like Olivia Rodrigo’s good 4 u, The Weeknd’s Blinding Lights, Ne-Yo’s Closer, and Don Toliver’s After Party land in the far upper-right quadrant: - Tempo & Energy Contrast: These songs feature rapid tempos (126–171 BPM) and high energy (66–77). - Listening Context: They are engineered for high-arousal environments like workouts, parties, or driving anthems. While enjoyable in specific moods, their aggressive compression and rapid rhythm make them less suited for focused daily listening than the mellow warmth of the Top 5.


4. Popularity, Meaning, and Mood

Popularity: Mainstream chart-toppers like Blinding Lights and good 4 u boast popularity scores around 90. In contrast, the Top 5 tracks sit comfortably in the 65–76 popularity range, showing a preference for artist-first indie releases over viral radio hits.
Meaning & Mood: The Top 5 songs explore nuanced emotional themes—vulnerability, yearning, and relationship reflections (Evergreen, Give You the World)—paired with laid-back, bittersweet chords that create comforting, repeatable listening experiences.



5. Contextualizing Against the Broader Music Landscape
The 5,000 background tracks sampled from Spotify illustrate how music fans consume across Spotify: - High-octane rock anthems like Led Zeppelin’s Whole Lotta Love push energy past 90. - Bright pop tracks like Doja Cat’s Say So, Justin Bieber’s One Less Lonely Girl, and Paramore’s Hard Times spread between 85–120 BPM with energy levels from 67 to 82. - Intimate late-night hip-hop like Drake’s Marvins Room drops to 26 energy at 112 BPM.
Against this vast 5,000-song landscape, the Top 5 forms a remarkably tight, intentional cluster. It demonstrates that the core listening preference is neither chaotic nor extreme: it consistently gravitates toward warm, mid-tempo, medium-energy tracks with heartfelt storytelling.

title: Conclusion
text:
This study analyzed personal listening habits by examining the sonic attributes of my Top 5 Spotify tracks alongside comparison songs and a 5,000-track sample of the Spotify catalog.
The central finding is that daily listening habits are highly deliberate: rather than choosing music randomly across Spotify’s broad acoustic spectrum, my most-played tracks consistently converge on a specific sweet spot defined by rhythmic stability, low listening fatigue, and emotional resonance.

title: Conclusion
text:
Evidence from the Graph
The scatter plot in the Visualization tab reveals three clear graphical patterns:

Tight Cluster Pocket: The Top 5 songs (SQUEEZE, Oh Yeah?, WALLFLOWER, Give You the World, and Evergreen) occupy a compact region defined by 75–92 BPM and 30–52 energy.
Contrast with Catalog Dispersion: The 5,000 background tracks spread widely across the entire plot—from high-octane rock anthems like Led Zeppelin’s Whole Lotta Love (energy > 90) to upbeat pop tracks like Paramore’s Hard Times (120 BPM, 82 energy). In contrast, the Top 5 avoids extremes.
Distance from High-Arousal Outliers: Chart-topping tracks like Blinding Lights (171 BPM, 73 energy) and good 4 u (167 BPM, 66 energy) sit in the far upper-right quadrant, visibly isolated from the Top 5 cluster.

title: Conclusion
text:
Evidence from Spotify Platform Metrics
Spotify’s audio feature algorithms and catalog data provide quantitative backing for these listening patterns:

Popularity Index (65–76 vs. 90+): Mainstream viral hits like Blinding Lights (93) and good 4 u (89) dominate global charts, but the Top 5 songs sit comfortably in the 65–76 popularity tier. This indicates a preference for dedicated artist catalog cuts over radio-promoted hits.
Valence & Mood Complexity: Spotify’s valence scores for the Top 5 range between 32 and 65, reflecting bittersweet, emotionally nuanced tones rather than hyper-positive party pop.
Replay Optimization: Low-to-moderate energy levels (30–52) produce minimal sonic compression and ear fatigue. Combined with steady, mid-tempo grooves, these characteristics make the Top 5 ideal for continuous, daily background listening, study, and reflection.
